note: STRICT-003 isolate writable state, recorded in the declared Linux environment. The action's world is built from tmpfs mounts: the workspace is the one writable location, the store is remounted read-only after its contents are copied in, and /tmp is a fresh tmpfs rather than the host's. The case asserts both halves - a write to the declared workspace succeeds, and a write to the store is refused - so a sandbox that made everything read-only would fail it. Fault proof: leaving the store writable makes the store write succeed and the case fail (exit 1); the revert restored the exact line and no FAULT markers remain. Ordering is load-bearing and documented: a mount cannot be created inside a read-only filesystem, so the read-only remounts come after everything is mounted, and remounting a parent does not affect a child mount.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
